title: Koszul complex is perfect on affine scheme
statement: Let A be a commutative ring, r a natural number, f : Fin r → A, and e ≥ 1. Write X = Spec A [def-pc-scheme], I for the deleted, shifted Koszul complex on the powers f(i)^e [def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex, def-pc-shifted-koszul-augmentation]. The derived object of the termwise associated sheaf of I is perfect on X [def-pc-perfect-complex].

source.place: Tag 08CX (perfect-section-koszul), definition of $I^\bullet$ and the assertion that $I_e\to\mathcal O_X$ becomes an isomorphism on $U$

proof.text: For each e, the Koszul complex K^\bullet(f_1^e,\ldots,f_r^e) is concentrated in the finite range [-r,0], and its term in degree -j is the finite free A-module \bigwedge_A^j A^{\oplus r}. The shifted complex I^\bullet has the same finite-free terms (with the indicated shift and sign change), so its associated complex on X=Spec(A) is strictly perfect. By the affine characterization in [def-pc-perfect-complex], the object I_e is perfect.

theorem affine_perfect_koszul_principal_unit_perfect
    (A : Type a) [CommRing A] (r : ℕ) (f : Fin r → A) (e : ℕ) (he : 1 ≤ e)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{b}
      (SheafOfModules.{a} (moduleRings (Spec (.of A)).toRingedSpace))]
    [∀ U : (Spec (.of A)).Opens,
      HasDerivedCategory.{b}
        (SheafOfModules.{a} ((moduleRings (Spec (.of A)).toRingedSpace).over U))] :
    Scheme.IsPerfect (Spec (.of A))
      (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
        ((@Functor.mapHomologicalComplex ℤ (ModuleCat.{a} A)
          (SheafOfModules.{a} (moduleRings (Spec (.of A)).toRingedSpace))
          _ _ _ _ (tilde.functor (.of A))
          ⟨fun _ _ ↦ tilde.map_zero⟩ (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj
          (shiftedKoszulComplex A r (fun i ↦ f i ^ e))))
